---
title: "How this was built"
description: "A human directing AI agents, with the direction kept as an auditable record — shown here, not linked."
---

Tributary is two projects sharing one repository. The data science build is
the visible one. The primary one is the working method: a human directing AI
agents to produce real, reviewable work, and keeping enough of a record that
an outside evaluator can decompose who contributed what. This page shows the
method in two parts. **The harness** is the reusable system: what an agent
loads before it starts, what events force a record, how a decision is put to
the human, and what closes a phase. **The records** are its outputs: who
authored each commit, one business problem traced from the human's seed to
the published number, one decision the human amended rather than ratified,
and four prompts with what each one changed.

Every vignette below ends in a work-product consequence — a number on another
page of this site, a file in the repository, or a rule that bound every later
session. Nothing here is a description of the logging schema.

## The harness

### How a phase runs

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "The operating loop every session runs under (meta/conventions.md Section 3; meta/charter.md Section 2). Agents propose; the human ratifies, amends, or rejects; a phase closes only when its records are current."
flowchart TD
  S["Session start<br/>CLAUDE.md auto-loads; the agent reads the conventions and the knowledge graph,<br/>then states which phase and design sections govern the session"] --> W["Work under the twelve standing agreements"]
  W --> T{"Trigger table fires?"}
  T -- "human corrects a misread" --> INT["interventions.md entry, classified"]
  T -- "choice between real alternatives" --> DEC["decisions.md entry"]
  T -- "a prompt shaped an artifact" --> PR["prompts.md candidate, verbatim minus marked redactions"]
  T -- "repo structure changed" --> G["graph.yaml diff in the same commit"]
  T -- "design doc changed" --> CL["design.md changelog row citing the trigger id"]
  INT & DEC & PR & G & CL --> E["Session end: the agent drafts candidate records<br/>as explicit asks: what was decided, the question, consequences, recommendation"]
  E --> R{"Human"}
  R -- "accept" --> C["Commit with a Provenance trailer: H, HD, or A"]
  R -- "amend" --> W
  R -- "reject" --> X["Record kept and marked rejected"]
  C --> GATE{"Phase gate"}
  GATE -- "local exit criteria met AND logs current, graph validates, provenance recorded" --> NEXT["Handoff note for the next phase"]
  GATE -- "not met" --> W
  classDef human fill:#f1e6d4,stroke:#8a5a2b,color:#1f2933;
  class R,GATE human;
```

Agents in this repository do not start from a blank prompt. `CLAUDE.md` is
auto-loaded and points at a read-first list: the
[twelve working agreements](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/conventions.md)
(quality over development cost, no invented company names, honesty over
flash, comment the code, index the repository for agents), the
[knowledge graph](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/graph/graph.yaml)
that indexes every document, package, silo and phase and is validated in CI on
every push, and the
[design document](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/docs/design.md)
that seeded the build and is kept alive by a changelog in which every row
cites the decision or intervention that caused it.

### The trigger table

The rule that keeps the record honest is mechanical: certain events during
work *require* a record, and the session does not end until the candidates
are drafted for the human to accept, edit, or reject.

| Event during work | Required record |
| --- | --- |
| The human corrects an agent misunderstanding of the design doc | `interventions.md` entry, with a classification (misread, ambiguity, overrule, omission, en-route fix) |
| The design doc changes for any reason | `design.md` changelog row citing an intervention or decision id |
| A choice is made between real alternatives | `decisions.md` entry |
| Repository structure changes | `graph.yaml` diff in the same commit |
| A prompt materially shaped an artifact | `prompts.md` candidate, verbatim minus marked redactions |
| Something off-topic is found and fixed | `interventions.md` entry flagged "en-route fix" |

### How a decision is put to the human

Early in Phase 1 the agent ended a session with "Pending your ratification:
C10, C15, C16, C17" and the human had to ask what was actually being
requested. The correction (intervention INT-015) became the standing form for
every decision request since, and it is the form the handoff notes for Phases
4, 5 and 6 open with:

1. one sentence stating what was decided and why;
2. the concrete question, usually accept / amend / reject;
3. what each answer entails downstream;
4. the agent's recommendation.

A bare list of ids is not a decision request. The consequence of that rule is
visible on this page: the decision rendered in full below ends in an explicit
ask, and the human's answer changed the work.

## The records

### Who authored what: provenance by phase

Every commit carries a trailer classifying its content: `H` (human-authored),
`HD` (human-directed: the agent drafted from specific human instructions and
the human edited and approved), or `A` (agent-drafted, human-reviewed). The
chart is generated from `git log` by a
[script in the repository](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/tools/provenance_by_phase.py),
so it cannot drift from the commits.

![Commits per phase by provenance level, generated from commit trailers.](../assets/img/provenance_by_phase.svg){fig-alt="Horizontal stacked bars, one per project phase, showing counts of human-directed and agent-drafted commits; no bar contains a human-authored segment."}

Read it plainly: **no commit is `H`**. The human's authored contribution
enters through the `HD` commits — the prompts, the ratification text, and on
two occasions the author's own industry data — rather than through commits of
the human's own. That is an honest description of how a director works with
agents, and the record says so rather than leaving a reader to infer it. Of
52 commits, 29 are `HD`, 19 are `A`, and 4 predate the harness; 21 carry a
`Directs:` trailer naming the prompt that produced them. Phase 1 (the
simulation engine) is the most human-directed phase; the Phase 7 site
performance passes were agent work.

### One business problem, end to end

The question the marketplace could not answer before unification: how many
distinct consumers do we actually have, and what does buying the same
consumer twice cost? The chain below is every record on the way to the
published answer, in order. It is rendered from the
[interaction ledger](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/logs/ledger.md),
a small index that links existing records rather than restating them.

{{< include _includes/chain_identity.qmd >}}

What the chain shows. The human seeded the idea ("impose/add unifying keys"
on simulated data); the agent turned it into a scoring mechanism. When the
agent's first entity-resolution run scored F1 0.976 and 0.997, it flagged
its own result as too clean and recommended turning the difficulty up; the
human did that, but not the way the agent proposed — the author supplied a
one-year leads-per-contact distribution from industry experience and a
channel-dependent drift mechanism, and moved the target band down to
0.8–0.9. The next run landed at 0.879 and 0.873 on the default dials. When the
resulting dashboards showed $40.0M of duplicate spend with no demand penalty,
the human called that "troublesome" and supplied a second table; the engine
learned buyer-side suppression, and the published figure became **$12.0M**
(5.7% of revenue) still paid for consumers bought within the prior 30 days,
against **635,579** resolved consumers behind 2.40M lead ids. Every number on
the [findings page](dashboards.qmd) sits downstream of those two human
inputs.

### Four prompts and what each one changed

The prompt log records prompts verbatim, minus marked redactions, when they
materially shaped an artifact. These four are the ones a reader of the
technical pages is standing on. Each is rendered from the log; the one-line
annotation names the consequence.

**P-005 — every data mutation made visible.** Consequence: the data-mutation
ledger convention in `calibration_spec.md`, applied to every profiling
notebook since; it immediately exposed a sentinel covering 4.3% of one
dataset's rows.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="P-005, verbatim from meta/logs/prompts.md"}
{{< include _includes/record_P-005.qmd >}}
:::

**P-008 — where the never-applier prospects come from.** Consequence: the
seven-channel acquisition layer with full-funnel unit economics, which is why
the [attribution dashboard](dashboards.qmd) has a channel that runs below
break-even and one that runs above 3x.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="P-008, verbatim from meta/logs/prompts.md"}
{{< include _includes/record_P-008.qmd >}}
:::

**P-010 — the author's repeat-application distribution.** Consequence: the
simulated world's heavy-tailed repeat behaviour (mean 3.8 applications per
person) and channel-dependent identity drift; the entity-resolution band
moved to 0.8–0.9; the raw table never entered the repository (its fitted form
did).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="P-010, verbatim minus one marked redaction"}
{{< include _includes/record_P-010.qmd >}}
:::

**P-011 — duplicates should win less and clear lower.** Consequence: buyer
demand responds to recency, the funded flag carries a modest price gradient,
overall sell-through moved from the invented ~60% to the source data's 49%,
and every headline number on this site changed.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="P-011, verbatim minus one marked redaction"}
{{< include _includes/record_P-011.qmd >}}
:::

### The corrections, kept

Sixteen interventions preceded this reframe, from the agent's fictional
company name (overruled as meaningless) and its default AI co-author trailer
(rejected in favour of the provenance trailers above) to the two that matter
most for the science: the agent labelled a valid out-of-domain estimate as
"wrong-sign" and the human reframed it (INT-013), and the agent then ratified
a parameter together with its verification gate without one line of
feasibility arithmetic — the gate falsified the parameter the same day and
the falsified record was kept and superseded, not rewritten (INT-014). The
seventeenth intervention is this page's reason for existing: after reading
the first release of this site start to finish, the human recorded that it
read like data engineering and that the method was asserted rather than
shown. The reframe was run through the harness like any other correction,
and its records are in the log.

the [intervention log](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/logs/interventions.md),
the [prompt log](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/logs/prompts.md),
the [interaction ledger](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/meta/logs/ledger.md),

It is the part of the project I would most want an evaluator to open.
